learning_outcomes.text: The student must demonstrate knowledge of the fundamental concepts that inspire the design of the various levels of a network system. In particular, the student must demonstrate understanding and ability to describe the communication protocols described in the course and the ability to understand the advantages, limitations, and tradeoffs of the studied technologies and protocols.

The student must demonstrate the ability to apply the learned techniques and knowledge to solve simple network configuration problems, protocol analysis, and network traffic traces. The student must also demonstrate the acquired ability to use simple software tools for network analysis and network system simulation.

syllabus_topics: Quality of Service in packet-switched networks
Datagram networks and virtual circuit networks
The TCP/IP protocol stack and the IETF
Distributed software development and the socket API and its use in C and Python languages
End-to-end techniques for error, flow, and congestion control
Unicast and multicast routing in intra-domain environment
Shared media access techniques in LAN environment
Interconnection of LANs: bridging and switching
Connecting LANs in a geographical network: access technologies
Local Network Management: addressing, NAT and DHCP services, VLAN services
Wireless LAN and PAN networks: 802.11 and Bluetooth technologies
assessment_rules: The exam consists of a written test and an oral test. The result of the written test is binding for access to the oral test. Written questions can be multiple choice and/or free response and/or numerical exercises.
bibliography: J. Kurose, K. Ross - Reti di calcolatori e Internet. Un approccio top-down. (7a ed.) - Pearson 2017
